--- title: Relational data and PostgreSQL — understand the model before connecting description: Evolve the in-memory task model, start an exclusively owned PostgreSQL cluster, distinguish processes, storage, databases and roles, and verify keys, constraints, NULL and recovery. --- import { getRelationalExample } from '@/lib/js2py-examples' ## 1. A database is not an upgraded JSON file The H-series in-memory API can answer HTTP requests, but two requests can read the same old state and overwrite each other's changes. Process exit loses memory. Replacing memory with a JSON file changes the storage location, not the coordination problem: who manages simultaneous writers, recovers a partially completed write, or rejects invalid data written by a different script? Files work well for small tools with explicit single-writer ownership; increasing their size does not gradually turn them into collaborative storage. A relational database delegates these responsibilities to a separate server: typed records, relationships, constraints applied to every writer, concurrency coordination, and commit/recovery protocols. It is not a library for editing a JSON file directly, and it does not discover your business rules or permissions automatically. D01 establishes the model and server; D02 teaches queries; D03 groups changes into transactions. | Chapter contract | Verifiable scope | | --- | --- | | Prerequisites | L00–L14 and H01–H06; exceptions, modules, files, tests and the in-memory HTTP lab, but no assumed SQL or operations experience | | New capabilities | Draw relationships; explain tables, rows, keys, constraints and NULL; distinguish processes, directories, databases, roles and connections | | Independent acceptance | Create the model in an isolated cluster, predict who rejects invalid records, and design keys and relationships for a new entity | | Exclusions | Docker, ORM, migrations framework, authentication, pools and production deployment; successful installation is not modeling proficiency | Download the [complete D01 lab](/learning-assets/js2py/d01-relational-data.zip) and work inside the extracted `d01-relational-data` directory. All SQL, server and file operations run locally, not in browser Python. Displayed source and the download use the same lab files. ## 2. Make field evolution an explicit design decision The H model, `id/title/minutes/done/note`, describes single-user in-memory tasks. We now need to express who created a task in which project. The following changes are deliberate. **This creates a new practice database; it does not migrate existing H-series data.** | Previous field or new need | Relational choice | Reason and limit | | --- | --- | --- | | id | bigint identity primary key | Database allocation, not an array position; neither consecutive IDs nor preservation of memory IDs is promised | | title | At most 120 characters, non-NULL, not only ASCII spaces | Application validation remains useful; the database protects the minimum invariant | | minutes | Retained nonnegative estimate | Useful for aggregation and concurrency; a retained extension, not a mandatory capstone field | | done | status: todo / doing / done | false can map to todo and true to done; doing is new; do not maintain two conflicting truths | | note | Nullable description, at most 2000 characters | NULL means not supplied; empty text means supplied but empty | | Collaboration | users, projects, project_members | A user row is not authentication, and membership does not implement API authorization | | Ownership/time | project_id, created_by, due_at, created_at, updated_at | Explicit references; timestamptz for instants, UTC display in lab connections | `users.login` identifies fixture people; this is not a login system. Password hashes, tokens and authentication versions are absent. Add those through later migrations rather than inventing fake default passwords for an ORM example. Here `updated_at` has an insertion default only. Update code must maintain it; the column's name does not make it automatic. ## 3. One row represents a fact; keys express relationships A table specifies columns and types. A row is one record, without an inherent position in storage or query output. A primary key is unique and non-NULL and identifies the record across reorderings. Using a UI array index would identify a different item after sorting. Identity generates candidate numbers; PRIMARY KEY enforces uniqueness. ```text users (1) ----< projects.created_by users (1) ----< project_members >---- (1) projects users (1) ----< tasks.created_by projects (1) ----< tasks.project_id ``` The `<` side can contain many rows. A project has many tasks; each task belongs to one project. Users and projects form a many-to-many relationship, represented by two one-to-many relationships through `project_members`. Its composite primary key `(project_id, user_id)` allows a particular user to join a particular project once, while still joining other projects. `role` describes that membership, not the user's global identity. A foreign key stores the other record's ID instead of copying a user object into each task. Copies could disagree after a rename: an update anomaly. D02 will use JOIN to retrieve display names. A database need not store the exact shape of your presentation JSON. All references use `ON DELETE RESTRICT`: a project with tasks or memberships cannot be deleted silently along with its dependents. A complete deletion policy belongs in an explicit service operation. Equally important, a foreign key proves existence, not that the creator is a member or that the current HTTP caller has permission. Cross-table rules such as requiring an owner or making that owner the creator are not fully guaranteed by this DDL.
Explanation answer: why not store member_ids on projects or copy project_name into every task? An array makes both per-membership roles and unique project/user pairs harder to express through the constraints introduced here. Copying project names introduces update anomalies. A membership row represents one fact; its composite key and two foreign keys each enforce a separate rule. This is not a ban on arrays or JSON: independently constrained, queryable facts benefit from explicit relations in this model.
## 4. Understand DDL and constraints before memorizing insert order DDL is SQL that defines structure. `CREATE TABLE` creates a table; declarations describe permitted values; commas separate columns or table constraints, and a semicolon ends a statement. This complete schema is identical in all three labs. No ORM prerequisite is needed. {getRelationalExample('sql/schema.sql')} Read from parents outward: users, then projects referencing users, then memberships and tasks. Definition order does not nest tables; the referenced table must exist. `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` means ordinary inserts omit id. `DEFAULT` supplies an omitted column, not an explicitly supplied NULL. Omitting status produces todo; supplying NULL violates NOT NULL. | Rule | What it rejects | What it does not replace | | --- | --- | --- | | NOT NULL | Missing NULL values | Does not reject empty text | | CHECK | A false row expression, such as negative minutes | Alone it does not reject an unknown result caused by NULL | | UNIQUE | Duplicate login identifiers | This schema is case-sensitive; alice and Alice differ | | PRIMARY KEY | Duplicate or NULL identity, possibly across columns | Does not mean the entire business record is complete | | FOREIGN KEY | A reference to a missing parent | Neither creates the parent nor proves authorization | | varchar(n) | An ordinary write exceeding the length | Not every application normalization rule | `btrim` removes ordinary spaces by default, not Python `strip()`'s entire Unicode whitespace set. The application may be stricter; do not claim identical validation. `timestamptz` represents an instant; display depends on the connection timezone and does not preserve the originally entered timezone name. The lab uses UTC and does not resolve product calendar or daylight-saving requirements. ## 5. NULL is neither empty text nor JavaScript undefined SQL NULL means missing or unknown. A Python driver usually reads it as `None`, but SQL comparison does not work like Python comparison: `NULL = NULL` is unknown, not true. WHERE retains only true conditions. Test missingness with `IS NULL`. Replacing every missing value with empty text destroys information. Observe that tasks 1 and 4 have NULL descriptions while task 2 has empty text. A `CHECK (minutes >= 0)` does not become false for NULL, so tasks also needs NOT NULL. The tests create a temporary CHECK-only table, actually insert NULL, and compare that success with the tasks rejection. Constraint names alone are not the lesson. ## 6. Six objects between installed software and a running database | Object | Responsibility | Common misconception | | --- | --- | --- | | Tool binaries | postgres is the server executable; psql is a command-line client | Running psql does not prove a server is running | | Server process | Accept connections, execute queries, coordinate concurrency and persistence | Python exiting does not stop the server | | Data directory / cluster | initdb creates catalogs and database storage; cluster here does not mean multiple machines | Never edit its binary files or initialize over an existing directory | | Database | A logical database within the cluster, named langshift_lab here | Not a separate OS process | | Role | PostgreSQL's permission identity; lab_student is an ordinary role | Not the OS username or a row of the users table | | Connection | Stateful client/server communication establishing a database session | A connection string is an address/options description, not a live connection or transaction | Data flows from terminal/driver through a socket to the server session, constraints and storage, then back as results or errors. A Unix socket is a local communication endpoint, not the database file. The port number also identifies the socket filename here, although TCP is disabled. A random administrator role bootstraps the cluster; ordinary SQL runs as non-superuser `lab_student`. Owning this practice database is not a production privilege design. ## 7. Prepare step by step without touching existing databases Verified **2026-09-28**. Fixed baseline: PostgreSQL **18.6** (official release date 2026-08-13), CPython **3.13.15**, uv **0.12.13**, pytest **8.4.2**, psycopg **3.3.6**. The macOS Homebrew tools already exist on this machine; no system installation is needed. Elsewhere, obtain matching binaries through the official PostgreSQL download entry and verify their paths. Installation on other operating systems was not tested; do not blindly reuse the Homebrew path. **Step one: inspect binaries, not default services.** `PG_BIN` is a directory, not a DSN. Do not use `brew services`, unqualified management commands without `-D`, or assumptions about who owns a service on port 5432. ```bash export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-python-20260928 export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-uv-cache-20260928 export PG_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin "$PG_BIN/postgres" --version "$PG_BIN/psql" --version "$PG_BIN/initdb" --version "$PG_BIN/pg_ctl" --version uv --version uv sync --locked uv run --locked python --version ``` All four PostgreSQL commands should contain `18.6 (Homebrew)`; uv should report 0.12.13 and Python 3.13.15. `uv sync --locked` creates this lab's `.venv` from a public-PyPI lockfile, without updating it or installing frontend dependencies. Stop on a version mismatch rather than mixing baselines. **Step two: allocate exclusive storage and start an exclusive process.** The controller automates explicit steps rather than replacing them with magic: allocate `/tmp/lsdb-*` with mkdtemp; set root and socket directories to 0700; write an ownership marker; initialize the new directory with `initdb -D`; set `listen_addresses = ''`; start with `pg_ctl` using an explicit data directory and log; create the role and database only through this socket. The random port and unique directory never reuse an existing service. ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py start uv run --locked python labctl.py status uv run --locked python labctl.py dsn uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/inspect.sql ``` The first start prints a random root, and status should show running as true. Reset prints the following fixed output. It deletes and recreates **this lab's four tables**; it is not read-only. Save your own SQL files before resetting an exercise. ```text schema + seed ready: users=2 projects=3 members=4 tasks=5 ``` **Step three: understand the address before opening a connection.** The DSN contains `host=/private/tmp/lsdb-.../socket`, a random port, `dbname=langshift_lab`, `user=lab_student`, UTC and timeout options. macOS may resolve /tmp to /private/tmp; the abbreviated address in this paragraph is not copyable configuration. There is no password because local trust is bounded by private directory permissions and disabled TCP. Processes under the same OS account, and root, are not isolated from it. This is emphatically not production trust guidance. Before connecting or resetting, the controller checks the marker, directory ownership, server data directory, system identifier and `server_version_num=180006`. It deliberately ignores DATABASE_URL. Do not redirect it to your own database. psql backslash commands are interpreted by the client, not by the SQL server. ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py psql ``` ```sql \conninfo SELECT current_database(), current_user; \dt \d tasks SELECT id, title, status, minutes FROM tasks ORDER BY id; \q ``` `\conninfo` shows the connection, `\dt` lists tables, `\d tasks` inspects constraints, and `\q` exits the client without stopping the server. A continuation prompt such as `langshift_lab-#` often means you have not terminated the statement with a semicolon. Ctrl+C abandons that input; rebuilding the cluster is not the remedy. ## 8. Populate the structure with observable facts {getRelationalExample('sql/seed.sql')} The seed relies on empty-table identities starting at 1, so use reset rather than pasting it repeatedly into an arbitrary database. Expect Alice and Bob, Launch/Docs/Empty, four memberships and five tasks. Empty has no tasks but does have an owner. A foreign-key integer makes the server verify a parent record; the number itself carries no inferred business meaning. {getRelationalExample('sql/inspect.sql')} Inspection renders NULL as `(null)` to distinguish empty text. Tasks appear as `Design API / Add tests / Ship demo / Read SQL / Write guide`, with minutes `30 / 45 / 15 / 20 / 40`. This is the current ordered seed, not a promise about queries without ORDER BY. ## 9. Deliberate failures: who rejects what, and what remains? Reset first, then execute the explicitly failing experiment. {getRelationalExample('sql/expected_failures.sql')} ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/expected_failures.sql uv run --locked pytest -q ``` The four INSERT statements fail at server execution: duplicate login gives `23505`, nonexistent user_id `23503`, negative minutes `23514`, NULL title `23502`. ERROR output is expected, not evidence that nothing ran. This file temporarily disables psql's stop-on-error behavior and proceeds statement by statement; the final task count remains 5. In psql's default autocommit mode each statement finishes independently, so a failed statement cannot undo an earlier independently committed statement. D03 tests grouping them into one rollback unit. Tests also cover overlong titles (`22001`) and deletion of a referenced project. In the **actual 18.6 run**, `ON DELETE RESTRICT` returns `RestrictViolation / 23001`; do not assume every referential error is `23503`. Inserting a nonexistent foreign key still yields `23503`. SQLSTATE is more suitable for precise assertions than localized message text.
Guided modification answer: to allow unknown estimates, should you only remove CHECK? No. NOT NULL prohibits NULL; CHECK prohibits negative values. Allowing unknown estimates requires removing NOT NULL while retaining the nonnegative CHECK, and reconsidering whether default 0 remains appropriate. Compare NULL, 0 and -1 in a separate practice table rather than silently changing the three-lab contract. Later aggregation must distinguish zero from unknown; coalescing both to zero requires an explicit business choice.
## 10. Independent variation: multiple comments on a task Design `task_comments` independently: each comment belongs to an existing task and is written by an existing user; body is nonblank and at most 500 characters; a user may comment on the same task multiple times; deleting a referenced task is initially restricted. Draw cardinalities, choose the key, write DDL and a successful INSERT, then produce missing-task and blank-body failures. Why is `(task_id, author_id)` not a suitable primary key? Open the answer only after attempting it. Explain each constraint; passing tests alone does not demonstrate understanding.
Independent variation reference and acceptance {getRelationalExample('answers/variant.sql')} Comments have their own identity and repeat authors are allowed, so use an independent identity primary key. The foreign keys protect task and author existence, not project permissions. `tests/test_variant.py` executes the reference DDL and checks both failures, then drops the exercise table so it does not interfere with model reset. This table is not part of the ORM baseline.
## 11. Shutdown, recovery and a resumable checkpoint ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py stop uv run --locked python labctl.py status uv run --locked python labctl.py start uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/inspect.sql uv run --locked python labctl.py stop ``` After checking markers and server identity, stop invokes `pg_ctl -m fast -w stop` against only its own `-D`: disconnect this cluster's clients, roll back uncommitted transactions, and shut down. Other clusters are untouched. Status should show `running: false` and `pg_ctl_status: 3`. Start reuses the data directory without reinitializing it. Without reset, committed records should remain. This is a normal stop/start persistence check, not a backup or disaster-recovery drill. Data and logs are retained for diagnosis. The OS may clean /tmp, so it is not durable long-term storage. Do not copy a live data directory as a backup, delete ownership markers to bypass protection, or kill every postgres process. | Symptom | First inspection | Recovery boundary | | --- | --- | --- | | Missing/wrong binaries | PG_BIN and all four version commands | No automatic system installation or service upgrade | | Connection refused/missing socket | This lab's status and root/server.log | Start only the owned cluster | | Marker/identity mismatch | .lab-state.json and the private marker | Reset and shutdown refuse; investigate instead of disabling checks | | Partial initialization | Start exception, private logs and status | Script attempts to stop only the directory just allocated; preserve evidence and do not reinitialize old storage | | Missing tables | Whether reset ran and which database is selected | Confirm the target before choosing a destructive reset | When pausing, record the lab directory, random root, last successful command, passed tests, outstanding SQLSTATE and next action. A useful checkpoint is schema/seed verified, 14 tests passing, cluster stopped. Resume with status/start rather than an automatic reset. ## 12. Acceptance and official references Without the answer, draw the four-table model, distinguish a database role from a business user, connect to your own database, predict at least three constraint failures, distinguish NULL from empty text, and prove committed data outlives Python memory through stop/start. The acceptance runner also rebuilds downloads from allowlists and executes against an exclusive cluster. MDX compilation does not prove these behaviors. Official references checked **2026-09-28**, using PostgreSQL 18 documentation and runtime 18.6: - [PostgreSQL 18.6 release notes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/): patch version and release date. - [Client/server architecture](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/tutorial-arch.html), [initdb](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/app-initdb.html), [pg_ctl](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/app-pg-ctl.html): objects and lifecycle. - [Constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-constraints.html), [error codes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/errcodes-appendix.html): relational rules and CHECK's NULL behavior. - [libpq connection parameters](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-connect.html), [official downloads](https://www.postgresql.org/download/): connection targets and tool distribution. Not validated: other OS installation, TCP/TLS or production roles, backup recovery, authentication/authorization and production capacity. None is an implicit promise of this lab.

# d01-relational-data — Relational models, database objects and constraints

Verified 2026-09-28. A standalone lab using real PostgreSQL, not SQLite or browser Python. The full three-language lesson is `module-21-relational-data`.

## Outcome and prerequisites

Prerequisites: L00–L14 and H01–H06; D02 additionally requires D01, D03 requires D02. D01 does not assume SQL or operations knowledge. Read the lesson's mechanisms before following this reproducibility guide; installation alone is not mastery.

This lab verifies relational models, database objects and constraints. `model-contract.json` records `d01-d03-v1`, and `sql/schema.sql` is the executable DDL. User fixtures are not login accounts. H's done explicitly becomes status (todo/doing/done), note becomes nullable description, and nonnegative estimate minutes is retained. Users, projects, memberships and time fields are new. No existing in-memory data is automatically migrated.

## Fixed environment, no system service installation

- PostgreSQL 18.6 (Homebrew here; actual server_version_num=180006), officially released 2026-08-13.
- CPython 3.13.15, uv 0.12.13, pytest 8.4.2, psycopg[binary] 3.3.6.
- requires-python >=3.13,<3.14; uv package=false; a real public-PyPI uv.lock.
- Only macOS/Homebrew execution was tested. Other OS installation, TCP/TLS and production configuration were not. No Docker, ORM, authentication or frontend dependencies.

Work inside extracted `d01-relational-data`, not its parent. Tools already exist on this machine. **Do not run brew services, connect to default port 5432, or initialize existing storage.**

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-python-20260928
export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-uv-cache-20260928
export PG_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin
"$PG_BIN/postgres" --version
"$PG_BIN/initdb" --version
"$PG_BIN/pg_ctl" --version
"$PG_BIN/psql" --version
uv --version
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked python --version
```

Stop on a version mismatch. PG_BIN is a binary directory. psql is the client, postgres the server, initdb creates new storage, and pg_ctl manages the explicitly selected data directory's process. Installed binaries, running processes and data directories are different objects.

## Own an isolated cluster and database

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py start
uv run --locked python labctl.py status
uv run --locked python labctl.py dsn
uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset
```

Start allocates a short `/tmp/lsdb-*` path (possibly displayed as /private/tmp on macOS), sets root/socket permissions to 0700, saves matching state and marker files, initializes new storage, disables TCP, chooses a private-socket port, and starts pg_ctl with explicit -D and server.log. A random administrator creates database langshift_lab and ordinary role lab_student. A database is a logical namespace inside the cluster; a role is a database identity, not a users-table record. The socket is an endpoint, a DSN describes the address/options, and a connection is an active session.

Passwordless local trust is for the private directory with TCP disabled only. Processes under the same OS account and root are not isolated. Never copy this policy into an exposed or production server. Ownership is checked before connection/reset/stop; SQL connections additionally verify server data directory, system identifier and version. DATABASE_URL is ignored and arbitrary remote DSNs are not accepted. Do not remove those protections.

Reset **destructively recreates the four owned lab tables**, printing `schema + seed ready: users=2 projects=3 members=4 tasks=5`. Every pytest case and D03 demo scenario also resets. Do not run competing runners or keep business data here. Stop/start retains committed data; OS cleanup of /tmp means this is still neither permanent storage nor backup.

## Execute, interpret and verify

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/inspect.sql
uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/expected_failures.sql
uv run --locked pytest -q
```

Expect **14 passed**, with variable duration. ERROR output in intentionally failing SQL is expected; unexpected command failure must not be ignored. D01 checks duplicate 23505, bad foreign key 23503, CHECK 23514, NULL 23502, length 22001 and this version's delete RESTRICT 23001. D02 stores attack payloads literally without dropping tasks, and rejects invalid sorting/pagination in Python. D03 checks second-step 23503, subsequent-query 25P02, zero residue after rollback, real read-committed [30,40], repeatable-read [30,30], lost update 37, atomic increments 42, a one-row uniqueness race, lock timeout 55P03, and old-snapshot update 40001 followed by a whole-unit retry to 42.

The lesson contains exact demo output. D02's fixed ID requires reset first; D03 resets each scenario itself. These tests are execution, not compilation: an actual server applies constraints, parameters, transactions and locks. Independent exercise references are in answers; attempt them before looking. They are not extra baseline schema or HTTP integration.

## File responsibilities

- labctl.py: exclusive startup, address/identity checks, reset, psql and stop; no global service management.
- sql/schema.sql and sql/seed.sql: identical three-lab schema and deterministic fixture; model-contract records the DDL hash.
- sql/*.sql: queries or explicitly labeled failure experiments.
- tests/ and conftest.py: reset only the owned database per case, including reference-variation execution.
- answers/: references for independent work, not the starting point.
- pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .python-version, .env.example: dependencies/configuration; env.example is documentation, not automatically loaded.
- Three READMEs, sources.json and model-contract.json: reproducibility, provenance and ORM handoff.
- FILES.json: packaged file allowlist; the repository's sibling ../d01-relational-data-files.json drives integration packaging. No data directories, .lab-state.json, .venv, caches or credentials belong in the archive.

## Safe shutdown and recovery

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py stop
uv run --locked python labctl.py status
uv run --locked python labctl.py start
uv run --locked python labctl.py stop
```

Stop checks the marker, PID-directory relationship and healthy server identity before fast shutdown of its explicit -D, then waits. Status reports running=false and pg_ctl_status=3. Fast shutdown disconnects this cluster's clients, rolls back uncommitted work and retains committed data/logs. It never signals unrelated postgres processes, invokes brew services or deletes directories. Start after stop resumes storage, not initdb.

For connection failure inspect status and the printed root's server.log; for version mismatch inspect PG_BIN; for missing tables check preparation. Ownership/identity mismatch refuses reset and stop: investigate rather than deleting markers or substituting a user database. Partial first startup attempts to stop only its newly allocated directory and preserves the error. Inspect status/logs before proceeding; never reinitialize old storage. When a health/identity check itself is impossible, the controller refuses rather than guessing. Never use killall as a fallback.

At a break, record lab path, root, last command, tests, SQLSTATE and next action. After OS cleanup of /tmp, begin with a fresh extraction rather than treating unmarked old data as a new cluster.

## Limits and official sources

Normal stop/start is not disaster recovery. No production backup restore, power loss, ambiguous network commit, full Serializable matrix, real deadlock, authentication, authorization, pooling or load test is claimed. Later ORM work must preserve constraint names/types and failure tests. updated_at is not automatic. Owner existence and creator authorization are not fully enforced by foreign keys.

Official sources checked 2026-09-28. psycopg's docs site returned 403, so the official repository's fixed 3.3.6 documentation sources were read. PostgreSQL 18 docs and the 18.6 release page were accessible.

核验日期：2026-09-28。独立下载实验，全部使用真实 PostgreSQL，不能用 SQLite 或浏览器 Python 替代。完整教材是 `module-21-relational-data` 的三语版本。

## 目标与前置

前置 L00–L14、H01–H06；D02 另需 D01，D03 另需 D02。D01 学习者不需提前会 SQL 或运维。先读教材中的机制解释再执行本文件；README 是可重建运行指南，不把安装成功当掌握。

本实验验收 关系模型、数据库对象和约束。模型版本 `d01-d03-v1`；`model-contract.json` 给出字段与 ORM 衔接，`sql/schema.sql` 是可执行 DDL。身份/权限尚未实现：users 是测试人员，不是可登录账号。旧 H 字段明确演进：done 变 status（todo/doing/done），note 变 description（可空），minutes 保留为非负估时；新增用户、项目、成员和时间字段。这不是对已有内存数据自动迁移。

## 固定环境，不安装系统服务

- PostgreSQL 18.6（本机 Homebrew，服务端实际 `server_version_num=180006`）；官方发布日期 2026-08-13。
- CPython 3.13.15，uv 0.12.13，pytest 8.4.2，psycopg[binary] 3.3.6。
- `requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"`；uv package=false；公共 PyPI 的真实 uv.lock。
- 仅 macOS/Homebrew 环境已实测；其他 OS 安装、TCP/TLS 和生产配置未实测。无 Docker、ORM、认证、前端依赖。

工作目录必须是解压后的 `d01-relational-data`，不是上级目录。此机器工具已有，**不要 brew services，不要连接默认 5432，不要初始化现有目录**。

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-python-20260928
export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-uv-cache-20260928
export PG_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin
"$PG_BIN/postgres" --version
"$PG_BIN/initdb" --version
"$PG_BIN/pg_ctl" --version
"$PG_BIN/psql" --version
uv --version
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked python --version
```

版本不匹配先停下。`PG_BIN` 是程序目录；`psql` 是客户端；`postgres` 是服务器；`initdb` 只创建新存储；`pg_ctl` 按明确目录启动/停止进程。安装物、运行进程、数据目录不是一件事。

## 认领独占集群与数据库

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py start
uv run --locked python labctl.py status
uv run --locked python labctl.py dsn
uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset
```

start 的具体顺序：新建短路径 `/tmp/lsdb-*`（macOS 可显示 /private/tmp）；目录和 socket 均 0700；保存匹配的 `.lab-state.json` 与目录 marker；initdb 新目录；关闭 TCP；为私有 socket 选端口；pg_ctl 用显式 -D 和 server.log 启动；随机管理角色建立 `langshift_lab` 数据库和普通 `lab_student` 角色。数据库是 cluster 内的逻辑命名空间，角色是数据库身份，不是 users 表的用户。Unix socket 是通信入口，DSN 是地址/选项，连接才是活动会话。

本地 trust 仅因目录私有且 TCP 禁止才用于无密码练习；同一 OS 用户下的进程和 root 不在隔离范围内，不能复制到公网或生产。连接、reset、stop 都验证所有权；SQL 连接还验证服务端数据目录、系统标识和版本。脚本忽略 DATABASE_URL，不接受任意远端 DSN；不要修改这些防护。

reset **有损重建自己数据库的四表**，打印 `schema + seed ready: users=2 projects=3 members=4 tasks=5`。每次 pytest、D03 demo 也会 reset，因此不要并行启动两个运行器，不要拿这里保存业务数据。停启不会 reset；系统可能清理 /tmp，所以它仍不是长期保存或备份方案。

## 运行、解释和验收

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/inspect.sql
uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/expected_failures.sql
uv run --locked pytest -q
```

应有 **14 passed**，耗时不固定。故意错误 SQL 的 ERROR 是预期；普通命令失败不能被忽略。D01：23505 重复、23503 坏外键、23514 CHECK、23502 NULL、22001 长度；本版本删除引用的 RESTRICT 是 23001。D02：注入载荷作为原字符串保存，tasks 不被删除；非法排序/分页在 Python 拒绝。D03：后步 23503，后续查询 25P02，rollback 后零残留；真实两连接的结果分别为读提交 [30,40]、可重复读 [30,30]、丢失更新 37、原子累加 42、唯一竞争一行、锁超时 55P03、旧快照更新冲突 40001 后完整重试 42。

`demo.py` 的输出以教材为准，D02 确定 ID 需要先 reset；D03 每个场景自己 reset。测试不是编译：实际启动的服务器执行了约束、参数和值转换、事务与锁。独立题参考在 answers 中，先自己尝试；不是主模型新增字段，也没有自动接入 HTTP。

## 文件职责

- `labctl.py`：独占启动、地址、身份验证、reset、psql、stop；无全局服务操作。
- `sql/schema.sql` / `sql/seed.sql`：三章相同结构与确定种子；DDL 哈希在 model-contract。
- `sql/*.sql`：本章查询或明确标记的失败实验。
- `tests/`、`conftest.py`：每例重置自己的数据库；参考变式也执行验证。
- `answers/`：独立题参考，不要先抄。
- `pyproject.toml`、`uv.lock`、`.python-version`、`.env.example`：依赖与配置；env.example 仅文档，不自动加载。
- `README.md`、`README.zh-cn.md`、`README.zh-tw.md`、`sources.json`、`model-contract.json`：复现、来源和衔接。
- `FILES.json`：包内文件 allowlist；仓库同名 `../d01-relational-data-files.json` 用于主线打包。数据目录、.lab-state.json、.venv、cache 和凭证不进入包。

## 安全停机与恢复

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py stop
uv run --locked python labctl.py status
uv run --locked python labctl.py start
uv run --locked python labctl.py stop
```

stop 先核对 marker/PID 目录/健康服务器身份，然后对自己的 -D 执行 fast shutdown 并等待；status 返回 running=false、pg_ctl_status=3。fast 会断开本集群连接并回滚未提交事务，保留提交数据与日志；不对其他 postgres 发信号，不 brew services，也不删目录。停止后重新 start 是恢复同一存储，不是 initdb。

若连接失败先查 status 与所打印 root 的 server.log；若版本错查 PG_BIN；若缺表确认是否准备数据；若 marker/服务器身份不符则拒绝重置与停止，必须查明原因，不能删除 marker 或改成用户数据库来绕过。首次启动中途失败会尝试只停止刚分配目录，异常保留，后续先查 status 和日志，不对旧目录再 initdb。若健康检查也无法完成，控制脚本宁可拒绝；不要用 killall 兜底。

暂停时保存目录、root、最后成功命令、测试结果、失败错误码和下次第一步。/tmp 自动清理后应从全新解压目录开始；不要拿无 marker 的旧数据冒充新集群。

## 边界与官方来源

正常停启持久性不是灾难恢复。本实验没做生产备份/恢复、断电、提交时断网、Serializable 全矩阵、真实死锁、认证、权限、连接池或容量压测。后续 ORM 应保留约束名称/类型和失败测试；updated_at 不自动更新；至少一个负责人和创建者的项目权限不是外键保证的。

"""Own one disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 cluster; never use DATABASE_URL.

All destructive operations are restricted to our marker-checked /tmp directory.
Stop retains files for recovery. Nothing invokes brew services, kill or rm -rf.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import tempfile

import psycopg
from psycopg.conninfo import make_conninfo

LAB = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
STATE = LAB / ".lab-state.json"
MARKER = "langshift-owned-cluster.json"
VERSION_NUM = 180006


def run(*args, check=True):
    result = subprocess.run(args, check=False, text=True, capture_output=True)
    if check and result.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{Path(args[0]).name} exited {result.returncode}:\n"
            f"{result.stdout}{result.stderr}"
        )
    return result


def load_state():
    if STATE.is_symlink():
        raise RuntimeError("Refusing a symlink state file")
    if not STATE.exists():
        raise RuntimeError("No owned cluster. Run labctl.py start first")
    state = json.loads(STATE.read_text())
    root = Path(state["root"])
    if root.is_symlink() or root.resolve().parent != Path("/tmp").resolve():
        raise RuntimeError("Refusing a cluster outside the owned /tmp root")
    if not root.name.startswith("lsdb-"):
        raise RuntimeError("Unexpected cluster directory name")
    metadata = root.stat()
    if metadata.st_uid != os.getuid() or stat.S_IMODE(metadata.st_mode) != 0o700:
        raise RuntimeError("Cluster root must be owned by this OS user, mode 0700")
    marker = root / MARKER
    if marker.is_symlink() or json.loads(marker.read_text()) != state:
        raise RuntimeError("Ownership marker mismatch; no database action performed")
    if state["lab"] != str(LAB):
        raise RuntimeError("This cluster belongs to a different lab directory")
    for child in ("data", "socket"):
        path = root / child
        if path.is_symlink() or path.resolve().parent != root.resolve():
            raise RuntimeError("Refusing redirected cluster paths")
    return state


def raw_dsn(state, admin=False):
    return make_conninfo(
        host=str(Path(state["root"]) / "socket"), port=state["port"],
        dbname="langshift_lab", user=state["admin"] if admin else "lab_student",
        connect_timeout=3, application_name=LAB.name,
        options="-c timezone=UTC -c statement_timeout=8000 -c lock_timeout=3000",
    )


def check_pid_file(state):
    root = Path(state["root"])
    pid_file = root / "data/postmaster.pid"
    if pid_file.is_symlink():
        raise RuntimeError("Refusing redirected PID file")
    if pid_file.exists():
        lines = pid_file.read_text().splitlines()
        if (Path(lines[1]).resolve() != (root / "data").resolve()
                or lines[3] != str(state["port"])
                or Path(lines[4]).resolve() != (root / "socket").resolve()):
            raise RuntimeError("PID file does not describe the owned server")


def verify_server(state):
    check_pid_file(state)
    with psycopg.connect(raw_dsn(state, admin=True), autocommit=True) as conn:
        actual = conn.execute("""
            SELECT current_setting('data_directory'),
                   current_setting('server_version_num')::int,
                   system_identifier::text
            FROM pg_control_system()
        """).fetchone()
    if (Path(actual[0]).resolve() != Path(state["root"]) / "data"
            or actual[1] != VERSION_NUM
            or actual[2] != state["system_identifier"]):
        raise RuntimeError("Wrong server identity/version; refusing SQL")


def connect(*, autocommit=False):
    state = load_state()
    verify_server(state)
    return psycopg.connect(raw_dsn(state), autocommit=autocommit)


def start():
    if STATE.exists() or STATE.is_symlink():
        state = load_state()
        check_pid_file(state)
        result = run(str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "pg_ctl"), "-D",
                     str(Path(state["root"]) / "data"), "status", check=False)
        if result.returncode == 3:
            run(str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "pg_ctl"), "-D",
                str(Path(state["root"]) / "data"), "-l",
                str(Path(state["root"]) / "server.log"), "-w", "-t", "15", "start")
        elif result.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(result.stderr or result.stdout)
        verify_server(state)
        print("owned cluster ready (existing data retained)")
        return
    default = Path(shutil.which("initdb") or "/opt/homebrew/bin/initdb").parent
    pg_bin = Path(os.environ.get("PG_BIN", str(default))).resolve()
    for tool in ("postgres", "initdb", "pg_ctl", "psql"):
        version = run(str(pg_bin / tool), "--version").stdout.strip()
        if " 18.6" not in version:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Expected PostgreSQL 18.6: {version}")
    root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="lsdb-", dir="/tmp")).resolve()
    root.chmod(0o700)
    (root / "socket").mkdir(mode=0o700)
    state = {
        "root": str(root), "lab": str(LAB), "token": secrets.token_hex(16),
        "admin": "lab_admin_" + secrets.token_hex(6), "pg_bin": str(pg_bin),
        "port": 49152 + secrets.randbelow(12000),
    }
    # Persist ownership before starting so partial failures remain recoverable.
    def save():
        text = json.dumps(state, indent=2) + "\n"
        (root / MARKER).write_text(text)
        STATE.write_text(text)
        STATE.chmod(0o600)
    save()
    try:
        run(str(pg_bin / "initdb"), "-D", str(root / "data"), "-U", state["admin"],
            "--auth-local=trust", "--auth-host=reject", "--encoding=UTF8", "--no-locale")
        with (root / "data/postgresql.conf").open("a") as config:
            config.write(f"\nlisten_addresses = ''\nport = {state['port']}\n")
            config.write(f"unix_socket_directories = '{root / 'socket'}'\n")
            config.write("unix_socket_permissions = 0700\ntimezone = 'UTC'\n")
        run(str(pg_bin / "pg_ctl"), "-D", str(root / "data"), "-l",
            str(root / "server.log"), "-w", "-t", "15", "start")
        admin_dsn = make_conninfo(raw_dsn(state, admin=True), dbname="postgres")
        with psycopg.connect(admin_dsn, autocommit=True) as conn:
            state["system_identifier"] = conn.execute(
                "SELECT system_identifier::text FROM pg_control_system()"
            ).fetchone()[0]
            save()
            conn.execute("CREATE ROLE lab_student LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE")
            conn.execute("CREATE DATABASE langshift_lab OWNER lab_student")
        verify_server(state)
    except BaseException:
        # This exact new root was allocated above; never stop any default service.
        run(str(pg_bin / "pg_ctl"), "-D", str(root / "data"),
            "-m", "fast", "-w", "-t", "15", "stop", check=False)
        raise
    print("owned cluster ready: PostgreSQL 18.6; TCP disabled")
    print(f"root={root}")


def reset():
    with connect() as conn:
        conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tasks, project_members, projects, users")
        conn.execute((LAB / "sql/schema.sql").read_text())
        conn.execute((LAB / "sql/seed.sql").read_text())


def stop():
    state = load_state()
    check_pid_file(state)
    pg_ctl = str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "pg_ctl")
    data = str(Path(state["root"]) / "data")
    result = run(pg_ctl, "-D", data, "status", check=False)
    if result.returncode == 3:
        print("owned cluster already stopped; files retained")
        return
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(result.stderr or result.stdout)
    # Validate server identity while healthy. If it cannot be checked, refuse.
    verify_server(state)
    print(run(pg_ctl, "-D", data, "-m", "fast", "-w", "-t", "15", "stop").stdout.strip())
    if run(pg_ctl, "-D", data, "status", check=False).returncode != 3:
        raise RuntimeError("Owned server did not stop")
    print("owned cluster stopped; pg_ctl status=3; files retained")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=["start", "status", "dsn", "reset", "stop", "psql"])
    parser.add_argument("--yes-reset", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--file")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "start":
        start()
    elif args.command == "stop":
        stop()
    elif args.command == "reset":
        if not args.yes_reset:
            parser.error("reset destroys only this lab's tables; require --yes-reset")
        reset()
        print("schema + seed ready: users=2 projects=3 members=4 tasks=5")
    elif args.command == "status":
        state = load_state()
        check_pid_file(state)
        result = run(str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "pg_ctl"), "-D",
                     str(Path(state["root"]) / "data"), "status", check=False)
        if result.returncode not in (0, 3):
            raise RuntimeError(result.stderr or result.stdout)
        print(json.dumps({"root": state["root"], "running": result.returncode == 0,
                          "pg_ctl_status": result.returncode}))
    else:
        state = load_state()
        verify_server(state)
        if args.command == "dsn":
            print(raw_dsn(state))
        else:
            command = [str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "psql"), "-X", raw_dsn(state),
                       "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-P", "pager=off"]
            if args.file:
                command += ["-f", str(Path(args.file).resolve())]
            subprocess.run(command, check=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
